items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Sol Yaged tried too but he wasn’t that good a clarinet player.

ctx.x: Didn’t you do a thing with Benny Goodman when Igor Stravinsky was around too? What was that like?

It was quite an experience. I think about it every once in a while. Benny was a difficult man to deal with, to work for. He was Jewish but he was Adolph Hitler. He was mean, and different and callous and mean, and played his buns off. He was an inspiration when he played. But he didn’t like people. He didn’t care. There was a gesture that all of us knew meant go away. Not a nice man. Played better than anybody. And they won’t let his memory die. I just did a tour of Japan, a two week tour just recently a few…
Well you have to be fairly accomplished.
